Subject: Stressor run results (raw) — summary and recommended mitigations

Team —

We completed a 24h stress run in the dedicated staging pool Wed-Thu (window: 2028-03-07 22:00 PT → 2028-03-08 22:00 PT). Attached: raw CSV (stressor-results-20280307.csv) and a short notes log. High-level summary:

Findings:
- Baseline throughput: 3.1k tokens/sec sustained on the chosen fp16 model variant; int8 reduced cost by ~36% but increased P95 latency by ~18%.
- KV/prefix cache hit-rate was 62% for the long-turn summarization workload; miss storms during sudden fanout events caused temporary P95 spikes to ~1.4s.
- During an aggressive burst (simulated 2.5x peak concurrent), autoscaler responded in ~45s; routing fallback kicked in correctly to the low-cost variant but we observed a 12% increase in token-unit cost due to model spin-up inefficiencies and duplicated warmup tokens.

Recommendations:
1) Enable proactive small-batch pre-warming for predicted burst windows (we can wire this to Boreal's traffic predictor).
2) Increase prefix/KV cache TTL to 8 hours for long-turn sessions to improve hit-rate; add a passive refresh for very hot keys.
3) Use the int8 variant for background embedding-heavy workloads and reserve fp16 for interactive chat paths.
4) Add a canary rollout: 48h low-traffic window, then 1-week progressive ramp (10% → 50% → 100%).

Next steps: we can prepare a scripted canary playbook and a short SOW. Jordan — want me to add an estimated cost delta per month at 10% traffic?

Sergio Alvarez
Principal Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: stressor-results-20280307.csv
